title: Producing a singer cheaply in Mexico City
summary: Lee recorded a singer in Mexico City for half the Los Angeles cost, with Ernie Freeman's charts, charging only hotel and golf.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You mentioned earlier that you had recorded someone in Mexico City and there was something significant about facilities there.
Oh yes. I did. Well, when I was with ABC, there was a young lady who came in, and she had $30,000

and she wanted somebody -- someone sent her to me and told her I better give her some direction because she's running around with this $30,000 check -- and I have a reputation in the business as honest John, you know, so I'll try to direct somebody in the right direction.

So she wanted to sing, and she was a singer, as a matter of fact -- but she wanted to record here in L.A., and I gave her some names, of people, and she kept coming back and she says, "But why can't you do it?" And I kept saying to her, "Well, I don't really want to do it." And she said that she was gonna go to Mexico, and it was almost time for me to have a vacation, you know, so she said she was going to Mexico to work at this club.

So I said, "If you go to Mexico to work at that club, this is where you should record." I remember the man that got us the musicians when I was with Nat down there -- he was supposed to be the greatest musician in Mexico; everybody looks up to him in Mexico City.

I'm trying to think .. I'll get his name for you, but so she said, 'Well, would you come to Mexico and record me there?' I said, "Well, let me tell you now, we can make a deal -- because I'm going on vacation, and I was going to Mexico on vacation; Mexico City" -- but the $30,000 it would cost her here, I told her it wouldn't cost more than

$15,000 there -- which it would not. So she says, 'Well, what are you gonna charge me?' And I said, 'The only thing I will charge you for is you pick up my hotel tab and you pick up my golf tab.' That was all, you know. So anybody would say yes to that, but I don't know if she knew that it cost me $50 a day to play golf in Mexico City and I was there 3 weeks and I played every day. But you know, if it costs you $50 a day -- well, and I had a nice pad, but I recorded her there.

But my experience with the musicians there were unreal. Unreal. Ernie Freeman made all the charts for me, and I took the charts down there, and Ernie writes not easy for guitars, you know, and he wrote these guitar parts, and I took them down there and I recorded everything at once; I didn't lay tracks. You know, I didn't do rhythm sections and then the horns and strings -- I did everything at once, and the thing really turned out good. And the musicians were a pleasant surprise. They were unreal.

They walked in and they cut that music, and they were playing these rock things he had written just like you were in America playing it. So, you know, the world has become very, very small from shipping records, one country knows what another country is doing.
RCA. Very good. Just what we have here, they have it there. And if you want to go and see, where
I think the best recording facilities are, you got to go to Germany.
Munich, Hamburg -- they really -- I think they're kind of a little ahead of us, you know, in those types of things. I think they are.
